newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Tapie to leave jail - to face court.
newsitem.headline: France's Tapie to leave jail - to face court.

text.p: Fallen French tycoon-politician Bernard Tapie leaves his jail cell on Thursday, but only to face a court and another prison sentence.

The former cabinet minister and soccer boss, serving an eight-month term for rigging a soccer game, is appealing against a six-month sentence for fraud in connection with the management of his 74-metre (245 ft) four-mast yacht, the Phocea.

The flamboyant Tapie has tumbled from political and business stardom since 1993, when he rigged a league match to give his team Marseille an easy game before their successful European Cup final against AC Milan.
He has been declared bankrupt and ineligible for public office and banned from running a business. He has lost his seats in the French and European parliaments and entered prison last month.
His Paris mansion has been seized and his furniture was sold earlier this week, netting 4.2 million francs ($740,000) for his creditors. His yacht has been seized and is on sale.
Even his budding career as a film star is in jeopardy after a court last month turned down his application for semi-liberty to perform in a second film.
Court-appointed liquidators are trying to seize his three million francs ($585,000) earnings from his first film, "Men, Women: Instructions for Use" by director Claude Lelouch.
